quirks: Civil registration began 1 July 1837 at the Registration District level for births, marriages, and deaths; coverage was not universal before 1875 when penalties were introduced for non-compliance — some pre-1875 births, especially, may be unregistered.
West Bromwich was in the West Bromwich Registration District; Birmingham was in the Birmingham Registration District; searching by district name in GRO indexes is essential.

Both West Bromwich (Staffordshire) and Birmingham (Warwickshire) transferred to the new county of West Midlands in 1974; records created before 1974 are filed under the original county names — do not search 'West Midlands' record sets for pre-1974 events.

West Bromwich had an exceptionally strong Nonconformist presence — five Wesleyan chapels, four Independent chapels, two Baptist chapels, and a Roman Catholic church — so Anglican parish registers cover only a portion of baptisms; search nonconformist registers systematically.

Catholic records for St. Michael and Holy Angels, West Bromwich begin in 1832, but earlier entries are held at Walsall; check Walsall records for any Catholic events before the West Bromwich registers open.

The 1911 census is the most direct source for total children born to a couple: it records total children born alive, number still living, and number who died — search for Hannah Grice (nee Earnest) in 1911 first.
GRO indexes are quarterly; a birth registered after the quarter of birth will appear in the following quarter — if a birth is not found in the expected quarter, always check the next one.

In English working-class families pre-1900, the reuse of a child's given name almost always meant the first child of that name died before the second was given the same name — two children named 'John' in the GRO index likely means the first died in infancy.

West Midlands BMD (http://www.westmidlandsbmd.org.uk/) and Staffordshire BMD (http://www.staffordshirebmd.org.uk/) provide free regional indexes that may differ from the national FreeBMD index; use all three.

# Locality Guide: West Bromwich (Staffordshire) and Birmingham (Warwickshire), England (1860–1920)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **West Bromwich:** Ancient settlement; civil registration district from 1 July 1837. Part of Staffordshire until 1974 when it transferred to the new county of West Midlands.
- **Birmingham:** Ancient borough in Warwickshire; civil registration district from 1 July 1837. Transferred to West Midlands in 1974.
- **County seat / administrative center:** Stafford (Staffordshire); Warwick (Warwickshire)
- **Economy:** Heavy industry (iron, steel, metalworking, manufactured goods). West Bromwich was part of the Black Country; Birmingham was the principal manufacturing city of the Midlands.
- **Ethnic composition:** Predominantly English; significant Welsh and Irish migration into industrial areas.
- **Religious denominations:** Church of England; numerous Nonconformist bodies (Wesleyan Methodists — five chapels in West Bromwich alone — Independents, Baptists, Primitive Methodists); Roman Catholics (St. Michael and Holy Angels, West Bromwich); many denominations in Birmingham.
- **Key historical events:** Rapid industrial urbanization; WWI (1914–1918) with significant local military service.

## Boundary changes
- Both West Bromwich and Birmingham were stable within their historic counties throughout 1860–1920.
- In 1974, both were removed from Staffordshire and Warwickshire respectively and merged into the metropolitan county of West Midlands. Records created before 1974 are filed under the original counties.
- The civil registration district of West Bromwich was coterminous with the town throughout this period.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** 1 July 1837, at the Registration District level (West Bromwich Registration District; Birmingham Registration District). Source: [England Civil Registration](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Civil_Registration)
- **What exists:** Births, marriages, and deaths from 1837 to present, registered quarterly. Coverage was not universal before 1875; since 1875, penalties ensured near-complete compliance.
- **Where held:** Original registers at local register offices. National GRO quarterly index searchable at:
  - FamilySearch: [England and Wales Birth Registration Index, 1837–2008](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2285338) (free, indexed)
  - FamilySearch: [England and Wales Marriage Registration Index, 1837–2005](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2285732) (free, indexed)
  - FamilySearch: [England and Wales Death Registration Index, 1837–2007](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2285341) (free, indexed)
  - FreeBMD (http://freebmd.org.uk/): free national volunteer index, 1837–1983
  - Ancestry: [England & Wales, Civil Registration Birth Index, 1837–1915](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/8912/) (subscription)
- **Regional free indexes:** West Midlands BMD (http://www.westmidlandsbmd.org.uk/) covers West Bromwich and Birmingham district records; Staffordshire BMD (http://www.staffordshirebmd.org.uk/) covers other Staffordshire districts. Neither is complete for all years.
- **Ancestry:** [Staffordshire, England, Birth, Marriage and Death Indexes, 1837–2017](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/61709/) (subscription, indexed)
- **Gaps:** Some pre-1875 births were not registered. Events are indexed by the quarter registered, not the date of occurrence — check adjacent quarters.
- **Certificates:** Order from GRO (https://www.gro.gov.uk/) or local register office. Birth certificates name father, mother (maiden name), and informant.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Church of England (All Saints as the ancient parish from 1608, with daughter parishes Christ Church from 1829, Holy Trinity from 1841, St. Paul, St. Peter, and others); Wesleyan Methodist (five chapels in West Bromwich); Independent/Congregational (four chapels); Baptist (two chapels); Primitive Methodist; Roman Catholic (St. Michael and Holy Angels from 1832); many more in Birmingham.
- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, burials, confirmations. Many nonconformist registers include births and deaths rather than baptisms.
- **Where held:**
  - Church of England: Staffordshire Record Office (West Bromwich parishes); Library of Birmingham/Archives (Birmingham parishes)
  - Nonconformist pre-1837: The National Archives (most deposited centrally); also FamilySearch catalog koha:95994, koha:96001, koha:95998 for West Bromwich chapel registers
  - Catholic: Birmingham Archdiocesan Archives; FamilySearch has microfilmed St. Michael and Holy Angels records 1832–1995 (catalog entries koha:762327, koha:Church records for St. Michael and the Holy Angels)
  - FamilySearch: [England, Staffordshire, Church Records, 1538–1944](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2364451) — indexed + images (free)
  - Ancestry: [Birmingham, England, Church of England Baptisms, 1813–1919](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/4981) — indexed (subscription)
  - Ancestry: [Staffordshire, England, Church of England Births and Baptisms, 1813–1900](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/62292/) — indexed (subscription)
  - Ancestry: [Staffordshire, England, Church of England Marriages and Banns, 1754–1900](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/62293/) — indexed (subscription)
  - FamilySearch catalog: Bishop's transcripts of All Saints Church, 1676–1868 (catalog entry koha:327194; available at FamilySearch Centers)
- **Gaps:** No surviving parish registers are listed for West Bromwich St. James (formerly Hill Top). Some nonconformist registers were not deposited centrally.
- **Language:** English throughout.
- **Important note — Catholic records:** Catalog notes that for St. Michael and Holy Angels, 'Earlier entries can be found at Walsall.' Search Walsall for any Catholic baptisms before the West Bromwich records begin.

### Census records
- **Federal/national census:** Available for 1861–1921 (every decade), all indexed with images at FamilySearch and major subscription sites.
  - FamilySearch catalog entry koha:583890 confirms West Bromwich census returns 1841–1891 specifically online.
  - 1921 census at Ancestry and Findmypast (subscription).
  - **The 1911 census is essential for this research question:** it asked every married woman to state total children born alive, number still living, and number who died. This is the most direct evidence for identifying additional children. Source: [England Census](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Census)
- **State/provincial census:** None in England.
- **1939 Register:** Available at Ancestry and Findmypast (subscription); useful for older children's whereabouts in later life.
- **Missing:** The 1931 census was destroyed by fire in 1942. No 1941 census was taken.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills (testate), letters of administration (intestate), inventories, guardianship records.
- **Date range:** From 1837 for the civil Probate Act period; before 1858, under the Court of the Bishop of Lichfield (Episcopal Consistory).
- **Where held:** Pre-1858: Lichfield Joint Record Office. Post-1858: Principal Registry of the Family Division; indexed in the [England & Wales National Probate Calendar, 1858–1995](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1904) on Ancestry (subscription).

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Metes and bounds.
- **Types:** Deeds, land tax assessments. FamilySearch catalog entry koha:410643 covers land tax assessments for West Bromwich, 1772–1831 (available at FamilySearch Centers).
- **Where held:** Staffordshire Record Office (West Bromwich); Library of Birmingham/Archives (Birmingham).
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** Crown grants via local conveyances; deeds held at Staffordshire Record Office.

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** WWI (1914–1918); Boer War (1899–1902).
- **Record types:** Service records, pension records, medal rolls, casualty rolls.
- **Where held:** The National Archives, Kew; many online at FamilySearch, Ancestry, Findmypast.
- FamilySearch: [UK, World War I Service Records, 1914–1920](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2125045) — indexed + images (free)

### Cemetery records
- **Major cemeteries:** Heath Lane Cemetery, West Bromwich (burial registers 1859–1905 transcribed by FreeReg); Mayers Green Congregational Church graveyard (tombstone record at catalog koha:628392); Christ Church graveyard monumental inscriptions (catalog koha:482815); Birmingham city cemeteries — Witton, Yardley, Handsworth, Key Hill.
- **Online coverage:** Ancestry: [Birmingham, England Cemetery and Crematoria Records, 1836–2017](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/70926) (subscription); Deceased Online (http://www.deceasedonline.com/); FindAGrave; BillionGraves.
- **Physical records:** Sexton records at relevant local authorities.

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** Birmingham Daily Gazette (1862–1956), Birmingham Daily Post (1857–1999), Birmingham Mail (1871–1999), Aris's Birmingham Gazette (1741–1880) — all at Findmypast (subscription); British Newspaper Archive (http://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/).
- **Content value:** Obituaries, birth and marriage announcements, inquests.

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Record types:** Outgoing passenger lists, naturalization records.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch: [UK, Outgoing Passenger Lists, 1890–1960](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/4229516) — indexed + images (free).

# Locality Guide: West Bromwich (Staffordshire) and Birmingham (Warwickshire), England (1860–1920)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **West Bromwich:** Ancient settlement; civil registration district from 1 July 1837. Part of Staffordshire until 1974 when it transferred to the new county of West Midlands.
- **Birmingham:** Ancient borough in Warwickshire; civil registration district from 1 July 1837. Transferred to West Midlands in 1974.
- **County seat / administrative center:** Stafford (Staffordshire); Warwick (Warwickshire)
- **Economy:** Heavy industry (iron, steel, metalworking, manufactured goods). West Bromwich was part of the Black Country; Birmingham was the principal manufacturing city of the Midlands.
- **Ethnic composition:** Predominantly English; significant Welsh and Irish migration into industrial areas.
- **Religious denominations:** Church of England; Wesleyan Methodists (five chapels in West Bromwich alone); Independents (four chapels); Baptists (two chapels); Primitive Methodists; Roman Catholics (St. Michael and Holy Angels, West Bromwich from 1832); many denominations in Birmingham.
- **Key historical events:** Rapid industrial urbanization; WWI (1914–1918).

## Boundary changes
- Both places were stable within their historic counties throughout 1860–1920.
- In 1974, both transferred from their historic counties to the new metropolitan county of West Midlands. Records created before 1974 are filed under the original county names.
- The West Bromwich civil registration district was coterminous with the town throughout this period.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** 1 July 1837, national legislation administered through Registration Districts (West Bromwich Registration District; Birmingham Registration District). Source: [England Civil Registration](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Civil_Registration)

- **Where held:** Original registers at local register offices. National GRO quarterly index searchable at:

  - FamilySearch: [England and Wales Marriage Registration Index, 1837–2005](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2285732) (free, indexed)
  - FamilySearch: [England and Wales Death Registration Index, 1837–2007](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2285341) (free, indexed)
  - FreeBMD (http://freebmd.org.uk/): free national volunteer index, 1837–1983
  - West Midlands BMD (http://www.westmidlandsbmd.org.uk/): free regional index for West Bromwich and Birmingham
  - Staffordshire BMD (http://www.staffordshirebmd.org.uk/): free county index (not yet complete for all years)
  - Ancestry: [Staffordshire, England, Birth, Marriage and Death Indexes, 1837–2017](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/61709/) (subscription, indexed)
- **Gaps:** Some pre-1875 births were not registered. Events indexed by quarter registered, not date of occurrence.
- **Certificates:** Order from GRO (https://www.gro.gov.uk/) or local register office.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Church of England (All Saints as the ancient parish from 1608, with daughter parishes Christ Church from 1829, Holy Trinity from 1841, St. Paul, St. Peter, and others); Wesleyan Methodist; Independent/Congregational; Baptist; Primitive Methodist; Roman Catholic (St. Michael and Holy Angels from 1832); many more in Birmingham.
- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, burials, confirmations. Nonconformist registers often include births and deaths.
- **Where held:**
  - Church of England: Staffordshire Record Office (West Bromwich parishes); Library of Birmingham/Archives (Birmingham parishes)
  - Nonconformist pre-1837: The National Archives (most deposited centrally); also FamilySearch catalog koha:95994, koha:96001, koha:95998 for West Bromwich chapel registers (Mare's Green Chapel, The Old Meeting, Wesleyan Church)
  - Catholic: Birmingham Archdiocesan Archives (http://www.birminghamarchdiocesanarchives.org.uk/); FamilySearch has microfilmed St. Michael and Holy Angels records 1832–1995 (catalog entries koha:762327)

  - Ancestry: [Birmingham, England, Church of England Baptisms, 1813–1919](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/4981) — indexed (subscription)
  - Ancestry: [Staffordshire, England, Church of England Births and Baptisms, 1813–1900](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/62292/) — indexed (subscription)
  - FamilySearch catalog: Bishop's transcripts of All Saints Church (West Bromwich), 1676–1868 (catalog entry koha:327194; available at FamilySearch Centers)
- **Gaps:** No surviving parish registers listed for West Bromwich St. James (formerly Hill Top) in the FamilySearch Wiki. Some nonconformist registers were not deposited centrally.
- **Language:** English throughout.
- **Important note — Catholic records:** For St. Michael and Holy Angels, catalog notes 'Earlier entries can be found at Walsall.' Search Walsall for Catholic baptisms before the West Bromwich registers begin (1832).

- **Federal/national census:** 1861–1921, all indexed with images at FamilySearch and major subscription sites.

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** Birmingham Daily Gazette (1862–1956), Birmingham Daily Post (1857–1999), Birmingham Mail (1871–1999), Aris's Birmingham Gazette (1741–1880), Birmingham Suburban Times (1884–1901) — all at Findmypast (subscription); British Newspaper Archive (http://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/).
- **Content value:** Obituaries, birth and marriage announcements, inquests.

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Record types:** Outgoing passenger lists, naturalization records.
- FamilySearch: [UK, Outgoing Passenger Lists, 1890–1960](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/4229516) — indexed + images (free).
- **Content note:** Passenger lists record every person aboard, including infants and young children traveling with parents. Examine the full manifest for all family members.

- **Poor law records:** West Bromwich Poor Law Union (1834–1930); workhouse records at http://www.workhouses.org.uk/WestBromwich/.
- **Genealogical society:** Birmingham and Midland Society for Genealogy and Heraldry (http://www.bmsgh.org/) — the main society for Staffordshire, Warwickshire, and Worcestershire, holding compiled records and indexes.
